steps.name: Check Linux x86_64 host, KVM and free storage
Check the supported official Google Play SDK image and engine hashes
Reserve a unique AVD name, directory and unused control ports
Create fresh private userdata; never clone an existing phone identity
Configure four CPUs, 4096 MiB RAM and 6 GiB data storage
Reserve a persistent random serial and Luhn-valid synthetic IMEI
Prepare private Linux engines and the tested Android 17 S25 image
Pass the saved serial through the native emulator launch option
Apply the saved synthetic IMEI to the actual host modem responses
Retain authenticated ADB and token-protected local gRPC control
Install a persistent per-phone systemd boot service
Boot Android 17 with the S25 identity profile and no Magisk
Record the new phone's Android ID and preserve it on later boots
Verify SELinux Enforcing, secure ADB, non-debuggable guest and no su
Set display resolution to 1080 by 2340
Set display density to 416
Lock portrait orientation with rotation zero
Set manual brightness to 102
Set screen timeout to 2147483647 milliseconds
Set the friendly device name to Galaxy S25
Apply the saved GMT time-zone profile
Retain location mode 3 without inventing GPS coordinates
Enable mobile data and verify a validated cellular default network
Disable Wi-Fi
Set native modem voice and data to home registration
Set native battery to 83 percent, unplugged, discharging and good health
Reapply native battery, radio and saved settings after each boot
Install and hash-check the unchanged Duck Detector APK
Install additional explicitly selected apps
Configure a supplied per-phone proxy and matching GPS/time zone
Configure and verify a supplied camera feed using its measured app preview
Cold-boot again and verify identifiers, security, battery and connectivity
Save the profile snapshot, verification evidence and completion record
Complete Duck's startup checkpoint when needed and compare a fresh scan
